data.text/markdown:
Week 2 — Where data comes from: relevance and recency

Before you join anything, you need to know what each source is: who published it, what one row means (its grain), which column links it to other files (its join key), and what time period its numbers describe. That last one is the trap: a file downloaded today can describe 2021. This notebook reads every source the course offers and builds a source card for each, with the periods computed from the data itself — not from the file name or the web page. Your deliverable: choose 2–3 sources for your aggregator and fill in a provenance record for each (form at the bottom).

data.text/html: Source cards

Lesson 1 — one file, 5 different periods

Unplanned Hospital Visits holds 14 measures. They do not share a time window. If you put two of them side by side, you are comparing different years.

data.text/markdown:
Lesson 2 — "readmissions" from two CMS files are not the same years

  • HRRP (the readmissions penalty program): 07/2021 – 06/2024
  • Unplanned visits, READM_30_HF: 07/2023 – 06/2025
Both are CMS, both say "30-day heart-failure readmission". The HRRP window is older. If your question is about now, the newer file is more relevant; if it is about penalties, HRRP is the one that matters even though it is older. Relevance depends on your question.

Lesson 3 — release year is not data year

  • CDC PLACES is the 2025 release, but its year column says 2023. These are model-based estimates of the share of adults with a condition, not counts of patients.
  • ACS measures say 2017-2021: a five-year average that ended years before your hospital data.
  • PLACES covers 50 state codes; the ACS file covers 52. In the ACS file but not in this PLACES county file: KY, PA. Check the PLACES source page before you assume why — and before you assume your state is there.

data.text/html:
Lesson 4 — Fairfield is in Connecticut, and Connecticut changed its map

PLACES 2025 reports Connecticut as 9 planning regions; the ACS file still uses the 8 old counties. The course crosswalk puts the 8 hospitals in Fairfield County at FIPS 09001 — and 0 of them find a match in PLACES. Of all 36 Connecticut hospitals, 0 match PLACES. A county join for a Fairfield student would quietly drop every Connecticut hospital. Nothing errors. The rows are just gone. That is why week 3 counts rows after every join.
